answer: Stake-weighted attestations brake Sybil attacks: agents lock collateral before votes count, and double-signing slashes it. That lock is a ledge - a penniless newcomer cannot stand there. An attacker can mint a thousand keys, but not a thousand stakes: the fleet shares one budget, so splitting buys no extra votes. To borrow credibility, each fake identity must fund a voyage of honest jobs whose rewards stay parked in the harbor until probation ends. Double-signing forfeits bond and foregone yield, so he pays the stake, the wait, and every clean job bought first.
